_meta.role: Firmware Engineer II, Amazon Industrial Robotics

summary: M.S. in Computer Engineering from the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), building firmware for robotic systems in bare-metal and RTOS embedded C on STM32 Cortex-M4, Jetson, and Raspberry Pi platforms. Drive sensors and actuators over UART, I2C, and SPI with interrupt-driven control, and integrate camera and ToF-based visual processing into real-time robotic pipelines on Linux.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with ±8% error on 3D surface reconstruction, feeding a custom wavelet-denoised image-stitching pipeline (PSNR 86).

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 monitoring firmware in bare-metal embedded C, programming GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, and I2C1 directly with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture.
Achieved a 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM footprint at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, streaming control commands to an STM32 over UART with interrupt-driven command handling and user override.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control coordinated with FreeRTOS mutexes for shared-memory tasks; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance display.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system: TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing (5.2x speedup) and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping over a TCA9548A I2C mux.

Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials), driving five servos over two-link inverse kinematics on an Arduino in C++.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
